question.text: SEBI decides to conduct an inspection of the books and records of 'Narmada Credit Opportunities Fund' under SEBI (AIF) Regulations. What is the standard notice SEBI must give, and can inspection be conducted without notice?

answer.text: 30 days' notice is mandatory; no-notice inspection is not permitted under any circumstances
No notice is required for any inspection
60 days' notice is standard; inspection without notice requires a court order
10-day notice is standard under Regulation 24; however, in the interest of investors, SEBI may by written order direct inspection without notice

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 24 of SEBI (AIF) Regulations: SEBI shall give 10 days' notice before ordering inspection. However, in the interest of investors, SEBI may by written order direct inspection without such notice. Post-inspection, SEBI can direct: stop-launch orders, dispose/refund of assets, capital-market access prohibition, etc. The Trap: Options A/B/C misstate the notice period or the no-notice override clause. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C (Compliance) tests inspection procedures. XIX-C tests the specific 10-day/no-notice carve-out for AIFs. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Maintain an 'Inspection Readiness Pack': minute books, IC decisions, conflict registers, PIT database, CKYCR records, valuation files, FATCA/CRS registers, quarterly/annual reports. Nominate a senior officer as SEBI Liaison. A 10-day notice is NOT much time to assemble 7 years of records — be audit-ready always.
